_README: Curated laws for ds_contract, merged onto the primitive it names. Absence of an entry means nobody has written the law yet — NOT that anything is permitted. Keep this small: a rule here is a rule an agent will follow, and a stale one is worse than none. Every entry cites where the decision was taken. A key here is a COMPONENT ID — overrides merge onto the inventory walk by id, so an entry named after a token constant (KIOSK_UTILITY_SHEET) merges onto nothing and is law no agent can find. The one exception is `"kind": "recipe"` (ListPageRecipe): a multi-file pattern with no single component, which ds_contract serves as its own entry. A token's law lives in its docblock, which ds_tokens serves as the `use` sentence on that axis.

PhotoHoverPeek.useWhen: table thumbnail, row photo, product photo in a data table, hover to enlarge photo, image preview on hover, photo peek, zoom thumbnail, click photo full screen, open photo viewer from a row, catalog image in a list
PhotoHoverPeek.doNot: Do not hand-roll a hover enlargement sized by the image's own pixels (h-auto w-auto max-h-*): the peek is ONE fixed 18rem square, the photo contained, captioned 'Click to view full screen'. Do not open a bespoke lightbox on click — the default opens the shared PhotoViewerPortal (Unbox's viewer); pass onOpen only when the row has a richer photo set to open (the outbound ledger's LedgerPhotoViewer). Touch never peeks; a tap goes straight to full screen.
PhotoHoverPeek.law: src/design-system/components/PhotoHoverPeek.tsx (owner 2026-09-29). Mounted by RecordCard (CardPhoto), TriageRow and the outbound ledger's photo lane.

ContextualSidebar.useWhen: left sidebar, page sidebar, contextual sidebar, per-page nav, Vercel sidebar, lane door, parent nav vs child nav, back row, views list, sidebar filters, where do a page's views go, outbound sidebar, morph sidebar, sidebar mode, mode switcher, FBA mode, label intake mode, sidebar category heading, hairline divider, sidebar head order, sidebar top layout, where does the back button go, back button below search, find above back, page modes below back button, sidebar header stacking order, chat sidebar, chat threads in the sidebar, recent sessions, new chat button, view-less page panel, exceptions sidebar, exceptions domains, sidebar mode dropdown, page-declared modes
ContextualSidebar.doNot: The contextual sidebar is THE navigation surface for a desk's views (owner 2026-09-28): never add top inline tabs, a header tab row or a segmented view control in the page body instead. Do not list a lane's pages or a page's views in the page map (parent nav) once that lane is a door — no dropdown, no child rows; the lane is ONE row that opens its landing page. Do not put a page's verbs (Sync, Export, Add) in the sidebar — they sit in the desk header, top-right over the list they act on (NavPageActions); the one exception is a VIEW-LESS panel whose recents list IS the sidebar (Chat, `NAV_PAGE_DECLS[...].recentsPanel`), where the verbs ride the `‹` back row as glyph buttons (NavPanelActions, chord keycap on hover). Do not give a page its own sidebar component or row renderer — it DECLARES data (NAV_PAGE_DECLS, the recents surface registry) and the host paints it. Do not add a second search field: the pinned top row is the ONE field (NavFind) on every page — scoped to the page's list on a panel, the ⌘K palette's face elsewhere. Do not paint a page's views as body rows: they live behind the head's view switcher. Do not put saved views or filters behind a menu: they are the body's buttons. Do not reorder the head: the search field is never below `‹`, `‹` is never below the mode switcher, the mode switcher is never below the view switcher, and nothing (views, filters, page verbs) is inserted between them. Do not repeat the account / sign-in footer under every page panel; it lives on the page map.
ContextualSidebar.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/ContextualSidebar.tsx. SIDEBAR HEAD ORDER (operator 2026-09-27, every page panel, top → bottom, all pinned): 1) collapse · THE search field (NavFind: the page's list on a panel with a list — narrows it, grows right over the header while focused, locate pills under it — else the ⌘K everywhere face) — a pasted list rides INSIDE it — one token in the well, the rows in its dropdown (owner 2026-10-04); 2) `‹ <Lane/Page>` back row — `‹ <Lane>` on EVERY page of a door lane (a mode never gets a `‹ <Page>` row); 3) the MODE switcher (NavModeSwitcher) on EVERY page of a door lane (Shipping · FBA · Labels & docs; Deliveries · Sourcing), the same card in the same order (door first) with the page itself current — derived by the resolver from lane membership (`LANE_DOORS`, build.ts `modeLaneOf`), never declared per page, pinned by resolve.test 'every mode of a door lane…' (operator 2026-09-28) — OR a page's OWN modes (`NAV_PAGE_DECLS[page].modes`, owner 2026-09-28: Exceptions → Fulfillment · Inventory · Receiving), the same card and renderer via a `<page>.modes` section, the current domain's views under it in the view switcher; NEVER an 'all' mode (owner 2026-09-29: every URL lands on one category, a mode opens its first view) and `‹` stays the local peek (build.ts `pageModeRows`, pinned by resolve.test '/exceptions wears a mode card like Fulfillment…'); 4) the VIEW switcher (NavViewSwitcher). Mode = its own coloured card dropdown (NavModeSwitcher); view = NavSwitcherMenu. Both: HOVER teaches the keys in a card beside the sidebar (never shades the page); CLICK hangs an OVERLAY card under the block (the head never moves; Esc always closes it) with the choices as plain text. PAGE AGNOSTIC (operator 2026-09-27): any page whose desk mounts `DeskPageLayout bare` gets its header from the same NavContext (`useNavDeskHeader`, hydration-safe): the active view as title; with `viewKeys` declared, the title (`To ship ›`, grey bubble on hover) unfolds the views as pills starting right beside it (shortest pointer trip); they STICK after hover-off until Esc, a press outside, or a pill is chosen (NavKeyStrip / NavViewTitle). The body starts BELOW them with what changes often, as buttons: saved views, then filters. A slot that has no data is omitted without reordering the rest; after `‹` (the page map peek) the field stays pinned in the same place. ONE HOST (operator 2026-09-27): it is the desktop sidebar on EVERY page — a page with `rollout: contextual` gets its own panel, every other page (legacy rollout, scan stations) gets the page map with the page lit; never mount MasterNav/DashboardSidebar in the desktop column (it survives only in the phone-width drawer). LANE DOOR pattern (operator 2026-09-27): parent = the page map, one row per lane (`LANE_DOORS` in src/lib/nav/lanes.ts names the landing page; legacy spine SidebarNavList.renderLane and the resolver laneMap both honour it). Child = the contextual sidebar of EVERY page in the lane (the landing page and each other mode alike): pinned head (collapse · the search field, then `‹ <Lane>`), then the MODE switcher (NavModeSwitcher: the lane's pages as modes, door first, the current page lit — Outbound = Shipping · FBA · Labels & docs, Inbound = Deliveries · Sourcing; the resolver emits them as the `<page>.<lane>.modes` section), then the VIEW switcher (NavViewSwitcher: current view's glyph · label · count; the menu lists every view with NAV_VIEW_ICONS glyph, digit key, count). Body: the view's saved views FIRST as one-click preset blocks (Bookmark glyph, lit plate when the URL matches, hover × delete, `Save view` block only while unsaved filters are on; nothing when neither) — pinned at the top as buttons, never behind a menu — then NavFilters: a Sort row (the list's order; queues default to ship-by, soonest first), one row per staff ROLE (Assigned / Picked by / Packer / Tester on queues; Staff / Picked by / Packed by / Tested by on Shipped), one row per date range (Ship by, Ordered; Shipped with a time of day at each end), then the facet rows (closed rows, value chip, Reset pill riding the category hairline — Reset clears filters, never the sort; open options with count 0 sink to the end dimmed unless selected). All of it declared as NavControls (staff[], dateRanges[], sort) in NAV_PAGE_DECLS; every control param must be declared on its route and narrow the facet counts too. Categories are separated by hairlines, never text headings — map and panel alike. Page map order: top rows, lanes, Automations, Scan Stations LAST. Map ↔ contextual swap morphs in DesktopRouteShell (directional blur-slide, sidebarScopeSwap timing). The server contract (`GET /api/nav/context`) carries all of it, so Tauri gets the same IA. CHAT (operator 2026-09-27): Chat is the FIRST row of the page map and the ⌘K pin. `/ai-chat` is a view-less `recentsPanel` page: head = the search field over Chat's list ('Find chats', desk store, narrows the threads) · `‹ Chat`; `‹ Chat …… [+]` — New chat rides the back row (NavPanelActions, intent `ai-chat:new` registered by the page; hover discloses its ⌘⇧O / Ctrl+Shift+O keycaps — ⌘N is Chrome's new window, never advertised); body = its threads through NavRecentsList (`assistant.sessions`, ⌥1…⌥0 open the first ten). ACCOUNT FOOTER (operator 2026-09-27): the staff account bar (StaffAccountFooter) renders at the PARENT level only — the page map (legacy pages, and a panel's `‹` peek) — never under a page's own contextual panel.

NavFind.useWhen: global search, command K, Ctrl K, ⌘K button, find in this list, F to find, page search, table search in the sidebar, search hotkey, find button position, one search field, search scope, scope chip, search everywhere, merge search bars, two search fields, where is this order, which view holds it, locate pills, search overflow, search wider than the sidebar, paste many order numbers anywhere, search bar key card, hover the search field, paste a list into the search bar, ⌘⇧V paste a list
NavFind.doNot: A list page's Find is declared once — `NAV_PAGE_DECLS[page].search` — and the header field (bare F) takes it on ANY rollout; never an inline SearchField in the page body. Do not mount a second search field in the sidebar or header — there is ONE (NavFind). Do not paint the scope inside the field (no chip): the view switcher under it already names the list, and the field's width belongs to the operator's words. Do not clip the operator's text to the sidebar: while focused the page field grows RIGHT over the header (FindField overflowRight) — its 32px slot never moves anything. Do not open the palette as the page field is typed into (the list narrows live). Do not count a locate pill with a predicate its list does not use. Do not route scans or identify lookups through the page field — that is the palette's job. Do not write the desk-store Find to the URL. Do not mount a page field in the header while the sidebar is closed: the table bar's Find owns the list then. Do not hang anything right of the field (owner 2026-10-04): no `[›] N` list toggle, no `[⧉]` paste key, no right-side popout — a pasted list is ONE token inside the well and its rows live in the well's own dropdown. Do not teach F / ⌘K / ⌘⇧V in a HoverTooltip on the field or in the well: the hover key card is the field's only hint. Do not fire the paste-a-list chord inside a text field, or from a field that is not on screen (two NavFinds can mount).
NavFind.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavFind.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE field, search split by the ANSWER: PAGE = narrow the list on screen (`search.source` desk-store / url-param; bare `F` focuses; FindField overflowRight: while focused the well grows right to max(slot, 28rem) over the header's task/pin keys, z-50, the slot keeps 32px); CONTEXTUAL = where the text lives in the section — `search.locate` declares a locator, `GET /api/nav/locate?locator=&q=` answers per-bucket counts with each bucket list's OWN predicate, painted as pills in the panel under the field (tone dot · label · count, the list on screen pressed in, click = that bucket's href with the text kept as its desk Find); a locator whose records open on their own (support, /support) also returns its best matches as `q` entries (≤ NAV_LOCATE_MAX_MATCHES, the rest counted in `truncated`) and the panel lists them under the pills (NavLocateMatches — the SAME BulkRow face as a pasted number, no list verbs: status chip · `#id` · who · platform · order · subject; ↑↓ light one, ↵ opens the lit or single / exact match, click opens its recordHref); GLOBAL = the ⌘K palette: 'Search everywhere for “…”' row / ⌘↵ / Ctrl+↵ (openCommandBar({ query, scope: 'everywhere' }), CommandBarOpenDetail in app-events.ts; CommandBar.tsx belongs to the search session). With no list (identify, page map, header) the field is the palette's face (RollingHint 'Search' …, paste key); anything pasted there that is not a list opens the palette already searching. PASTE A LIST IN THE BAR (owner 2026-10-04): on EVERY face a paste of 2+ identifiers — ⌘V in the field, the well's paste key, a typed `A, B` + ↵, or PASTE_LIST_HOTKEY ⌘⇧V / Ctrl+Shift+V from anywhere outside a text field (key-registry.ts; the visible field only, hit-tested) — becomes the HELD list: LocatedFind → useNavBulkList(locate) (URL, so the page body's PastedNumbersLedger agrees), PlainFind / the everywhere face → useLocalBulkList('everywhere'). It shows as ONE token inside the well (FindToken `40 numbers ×`, AnimatedStat count) while the field text finds within the list ('Find in the pasted list'); the field's clear and ⌘⇧F clear text + list together. The list renders in the well's dropdown (FindField `drop` / FindPanel, NavBulkPanel): opens on focus from outside, ↓, the token or the chord; ↓ again walks into the rows; Esc / blur close it. One identifier keeps the old behaviour (page Find / palette query). The chord with no list on the clipboard (or a blocked read) lands in the field with the panel open: the held list, or a line that says to ⌘V. HOVER KEY CARD (owner 2026-10-04, find-key-card.ts `useFindKeyCard` / `findKeyRows`): mouse on the well for HINT_INTENT_MS (180ms) → KeyHintPopover enter="drop" hangs under the well, left-aligned, hotkey first: `[F]` + the page's Find (only where F is armed), `[mod][K]` Search everywhere, `[mod][Shift][V]` Paste a list — check each number (count = held list size). Hidden while the field has focus or its panel is open; a taught key pressed while it is up sinks its cap for one beat (publishKeyPressed, PRESS_BEAT_MS) before the card leaves. HEADER RECEDES (operator 2026-09-27): while a page field is grown (`[data-find-expanded]` in the DOM) every GlobalHeader zone fades to 30%, blurs 3px, scales 0.985 and stops taking the pointer (200ms ease-out, none under reduced motion) — GlobalHeader.tsx, one :root:has() variant, no state plumbing. FULL SCREEN (owner 2026-10-04: its OWN page, not a layer): `/search/list` (route tree node `pasted-list`, builder `pastedListHref({ refs, locator, status, back })`) — reached by the full-screen icon button at the TOP-LEFT of the list's header (bar panel and ⌘K palette alike; tooltip 'Open full screen', no key — ⌘⇧L is the browser's) or ↵ on the token; Esc / Back there returns to `back`. HOVER GROW + HEADER RECEDE (owner 2026-10-04): the page field AND the everywhere face grow to max(slot, 28rem) on mouse hover intent (180ms, `useHoverIntent`), focus or an open list — one `expanded` state that sets `[data-find-expanded]` on the well (`findWellGrowClass`: ease-in-out, 300ms in / 200ms out). GlobalHeader's RECEDE_WHILE_FINDING keys on that DOM attribute alone (no import): every header child except the one holding the field fades to 60%, scales .985 and blurs 5px, ease-in-out 300ms in / 200ms out; it STAYS receded while the field is focused or its panel is open (the calmest choice: no blur flicker as the pointer leaves a field the operator is typing in) and clears when all three end. This is a deliberate exception to NavSwitcherMenu's 'do not shade on hover' — a 180ms intent gate means a pass-through pointer never flashes the header. The key card still drops below on hover. FULL SCREEN: the held list's panel leads with an IconButton (Maximize, tooltip 'Open full screen', no key — ⌘⇧L is the browser's) → `pastedListHref`; Enter on the token too. The ⌘K palette holds a pasted 2+ list the same way (CommandBar `useLocalBulkList('everywhere')` + NavBulkPanel with `onClear`), crossfading with the results through CollapseItem on the findListPanel timing.

FindField.useWhen: find field, search field, search box, search bar, find bar, table search, data table find, find in this list, F to find, search placeholder animation, rolling placeholder, rotating hint text, animated placeholder, hint roll, text switching animation, paste button in search, paste to find, ⌘K face words, hover to reveal what a search does, held token in a search field, search dropdown panel, list in the search bar
FindField.doNot: Do not hand-roll a search input with its own draft/debounce, keycap, clear and placeholder — mount FindField. Do not animate a hint on page load or loop it while nobody is looking: it RESTS on its first phrase and rolls only on hover or focus. Do not change the timing outside the preset (0.22s spring, 1.8s hold, 180ms hover intent) — hover-only means brisk but readable. No bounce/overshoot and no blur on the roll. Do not use a native placeholder for the hint. Do not split the hint into per-word animation — the phrase rolls as one line. Do not hang the held list beside the well — it is `lead` (FindToken) + `drop` (FindPanel). Do not tooltip the field with its own keys (the caller's hover key card teaches them). Panel / token motion is ease-in-out tweens only (motionPresence.findListPanel / findListToken), never a spring. Do not paint the panel inside the well or fix its stacking with a z-index bump — it portals through AnchoredLayer.
FindField.law: src/design-system/components/FindField.tsx (operator 2026-09-27). ONE find well for every list: the sidebar search field in its page scope (NavFind), the global header's field when the sidebar is closed (GlobalHeaderSearch — owner 2026-09-28: never a second Find in the data-table bar), and any future table find. Anatomy left → right: Search glyph · `lead` (a keyed FindToken — a held pasted list, `40 numbers ×`, blur-in via motionPresence.findListToken; FindLead wraps it in AnimatePresence; ↵ on the focused token calls `onExpand` — the pasted list's own page) · field · paste key (ClipboardPaste; reads the clipboard through the same paste door as ⌘V) · clear (X, always FAR RIGHT, expanded or not — operator 2026-09-28; shows with text, or with a caller-held pasted list via `onClear`; ONE click clears both the text and the list). At rest the hint is gray and the paste key is hidden (takes no room); while looked at (hover / focus) the hint turns black and it shows — `findHintTone`, `PasteKey`, exported with `findWellClass` so the everywhere face wears the same parts (operator 2026-09-27). The panel under the well is FindPanel (exported; the everywhere face mounts it too), PORTALED to <body> through AnchoredLayer at the panelPopover band (2026-10-04: painted inside the well it sat under the page — the sidebar column's stacking context clipped it): bottom-start, matchWidth (the grown well) with min-w 28rem, flips/clamps to the viewport, max-height min(34rem, --anchored-available-height) with internal scroll, restoreFocus off, an outside press calls `onClose`; focus moving into the panel still counts as the field's (`focusStaysIn`, `panelRef`); its height opens with a fade (motionPresence.findListPanel, motionTransition.findListPanelOpen 0.32s / findListPanelClose 0.2s, easeInOutCubic) and pointer presses keep focus in the field. Top to bottom: `drop` while `dropOpen` (the caller's held list), then while it has focus and text `below` and, with `escalate`, the 'Search everywhere' row (its ⌘↵ is in that row's hover tooltip). `keyShortcuts` appends a caller-owned chord to the input's aria-keyshortcuts. HINT_INTENT_MS (180) is exported for the caller's hover key card. Optional `overflowRight`: the well leaves its 32px slot and grows right while focused (focus-within:w-[max(100%,28rem)], z-50) — the operator's words outrank the layout; the slot holds the space so nothing moves. HINT = RollingHint: rests on its first phrase ('Find' / ⌘K 'Search'); while the operator looks at it (pointer over it, or focus — `F`, a click; `useHintActivity`) the later phrases roll top → bottom ONE LINE AT A TIME (operator 2026-09-27: per line, never per word — read in one glance; motionPresence.findHintRoll on the whole phrase: opacity + y inside a soft masked edge, no blur; motionTransition.findHintRoll = critically damped spring, visualDuration 0.22s, bounce 0). Hover intent 180ms (a pointer passing through never rolls), then 1.8s per phrase. Leaving rolls back to the rest phrase; the next look resumes at the phrase after the last one shown. `findHints(label)` = ['Find', the list's 'Find …', 'Paste to find']. NavFind's everywhere face uses the same RollingHint + useHintActivity. Reduced motion keeps the swap, drops slide and blur. Sizes: `sidebar` (6px corner, caption) and `bar` (8px corner, body). TWO JOBS, ONE ROLL (operator 2026-09-27): a field with `escalate` rolls plain phrases — rest 'Find' → the list's 'Find …' → 'Search everywhere' → 'Paste to find'. Keys are NEVER painted in the well (owner 2026-10-03, hotkeys on hover): `F`, ⌘K and ⌘⇧V ride NavFind's hover key card (KeyHintPopover enter="drop", owner 2026-10-04 — the field has no tooltip of its own), `mod + ⇧ F` Clear's tooltip. The paste key never takes focus on pointerdown (a grown overflowRight well would slide it out from under the click). LOOK (operator 2026-09-27): white well, depth ONLY at the rim (inset hairline + inner edge shade; the middle stays white so black words read), 13px text-role-nav medium ink text-text-default, hint rests text-text-muted and turns text-text-default on look; pointer cursor at rest, text cursor once focused, accent-light selection; SEARCH_WELL_CORNER — soft 12px at rest, firms to the control corner when pressed or focused. No grain until the grain token axis lands (ds_tokens grain). THEMES: the well rim is mixed from its own ink (text-text-default → currentColor), so the edge shade holds in dark mode too. HOVER GROW (owner 2026-10-04): overflowRight wells grow on hover intent (`useHoverIntent`, mouse only, 180ms) as well as focus / an open list, via `findWellGrowClass(expanded)` (ease-in-out cubic, 300ms in / 200ms out) — the same `[data-find-expanded]` the header recedes on. FindPanel's height opens/closes through CollapseItem with `timing` = motionTransition.findListPanelOpen / findListPanelClose (tweens, no spring).

NavModeSwitcher.useWhen: sidebar mode switcher, page modes, lane modes, Shipping FBA Label intake switch, mode dropdown under the back button, where do a lane's pages go on its landing page, sidebar mode dropdown, page-declared modes, e.g. Exceptions domains (Fulfillment · Inventory · Receiving), a page's own sub-destinations as a dropdown card
NavModeSwitcher.doNot: Do not render modes as rows in the body or above `‹`. Do not give a lane of one reachable page a switcher (one page is no choice). Do not add counts to a LANE mode (a lane's modes are pages); a page's OWN modes (`NAV_PAGE_DECLS[page].modes`) carry their unfiltered count (facet context `<page>.<mode>`), amber when the glyph is `alertCount`. Do not add an 'all' / root mode to a page's own modes (owner 2026-09-29). Do not paint a page's own modes as plain body rows (the deleted NavBodyViews / childLevels shape) — declare `modes` and let this card render them.
NavModeSwitcher.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavModeSwitcher.tsx — its OWN dropdown, never NavSwitcherMenu (operator 2026-09-27). One raised card pinned DIRECTLY BELOW the `‹ <Lane>` back row, above the view switcher (see ContextualSidebar SIDEBAR HEAD ORDER). PARENT tier: the current mode's icon in its mode colour (its `SIDEBAR_PAGE_NAV` entry's `tone`: Shipping blue, FBA purple, Label intake teal), semibold, ⇅. HOVER (mouse, instant): KeyHintPopover beside the column — `[G] then` lead, rows `[S]⌂ Shipping · [F]⌂ FBA · [L]⌂ Label intake`, icons in their mode colours; never shades the page. CLICK / Enter / Space / ↓: an OVERLAY welded to the card — no gap: the card's square bottom and the overlay's square top share ONE hairline (absolute top-[calc(100%+1px)], z-dropdown, opacity fade only — the card keeps its height, nothing below moves) with the OTHER modes only — the current one is the card and is never listed twice; rows share the card's column (icon under icon, label under label), coloured, text only. ↑/↓ move; Esc ALWAYS closes it (window capture, wherever focus is) and refocuses the card if focus was inside; a press outside or a URL change closes it; the card is a LIST_KEY_OWNER. The resolver emits the modes as the `<page>.<lane>.modes` section. PAGE-DECLARED MODES (owner 2026-09-28, Exceptions): a page may declare `modes: { label }` in `NAV_PAGE_DECLS`; the resolver emits `<page>.modes` — each ungrouped child (Fulfillment · Inventory · Receiving, gated by `requiresAny`), its href its FIRST visible view, a secondary line naming its views — and stamps the current one `active`. There is NO 'all' mode (owner 2026-09-29: 'All exceptions is too much within one page' — each category gets its own table and resolver; `/exceptions` redirects every URL to one kind via `exceptionLanding`). This card renders it unchanged: the current mode from `active`, icons/tones from `NAV_VIEW_ICONS['<page>.<mode>']`, counts from `useViewCounts`. `G` letters come from `NAV_PAGE_GO_KEYS` (Exceptions: F · I · R) and are taught on the card's hover.

NavSwitcherMenu.useWhen: sidebar mode switcher, sidebar view switcher, Shipping FBA Label intake switch, FBM Allocate Exceptions Shipped switch, parent vs child nav, hover to see hotkeys, key hint card, click to expand inline, progressive disclosure of views, 1-9 view keys, G then S, go keys, view count chip, exceptions alert beacon
NavSwitcherMenu.doNot: Do not open a flyout menu to the right on hover — hover only TEACHES (a KeyHintCard, pointer-events-none, never pressed). Do not shade or dim the page on hover: a hover on the way to a click must never flash the screen. Do not paint keys in the click overlay — the keys were already seen on hover. Do not repeat `G` on every mode row: one `[G] then` lead, then `[S]`, `[F]`, `[L]`. Do not pad between a hint row's key and its icon: key far left, flush against the icon (gap-1). Do not paint a digit on a page that does not bind it (the page declares `viewKeys` in NAV_PAGE_DECLS → NavContext.viewKeys). Do not mark the current choice with a check — press it in (NAV_CHOICE_SELECTED_CLASS). Do not derive a view count from the filtered facets query. (Exception, owner 2026-10-04: the search field's hover-intent grow recedes the global header — NavFind law; the 180ms intent gate keeps a passing pointer from flashing it.)
NavSwitcherMenu.law: src/components/sidebar/contextual/NavSwitcherMenu.tsx (operator 2026-09-27, dogfood). CHILD tier only — the page VIEW (NavViewSwitcher: hairline block, medium, count chip, ⌄). The PARENT tier has its own card dropdown (NavModeSwitcher); the two never share one. HOVER (mouse, instant): KeyHintPopover beside the sidebar column, top-aligned with the block, popping like the AI chat context ring card (opacity + scale 0.96→1 on aiTransition.morph, origin top-left); rows are HOTKEY FIRST, key flush against icon — `[4]⌂ To ship`. No page shade. The pointer sweeps parent ↔ child and the card follows. CLICK / Enter / Space / ↓: an OVERLAY card welded to the block — no gap: the block's square bottom and the overlay's square top share ONE hairline (absolute top-[calc(100%+1px)], z-dropdown, opacity fade only — same edges as the block, row icons in the block's icon column; the block keeps its height, nothing below moves) with the OTHER views as text rows (icon · label · count) — the current view is the block and is never listed twice, the same rule as the parent card; ↑/↓ move; Esc ALWAYS closes it (window capture) and refocuses the block if focus was inside; a press outside or a URL change closes it; the host is a LIST_KEY_OWNER so the desk's record cursor stands down while focus is inside. Keys fire everywhere: bare 1–9 (NAV_PAGE_DECLS `viewKeys` → NavContext.viewKeys, pressed cap presses in for a beat via go-keys-store) and `G` then letter (NavGoKeys).

Uniformity comes from right-alignment plus `font-mono tabular-nums` — the right edge is the scanning line — not from falsifying the value. Do not square the cards with rounded-none or a raw rounded-* / border-radius integer. Panels use cornerClass('surface').
TriageScrollLayout.law: Operator 2026-08-30 — grouping is the scan; the edge rail is opt-in for a fixed-width pane, never a display metric of its own.

TriageScrollKnobs.useWhen: jump rail, edge knobs, section ticks, position readout, Grok-style nav, sticky section index
TriageScrollKnobs.doNot: Do not put a button row across the top of the form. Do not tween width or position when a tick becomes active — colour and weight only. Creates / fire-and-forget with no cached row still use useResourceMutation.
useOptimisticMutation.law: Operator 2026-08-30 — edits are optimistic; the paint is the feedback; failure is a bottom-right toast.

ProgressBar.useWhen: progress meter, completion bar, stage progress, percent done, N of M, goal against actual, segmented increments, Duolingo-style step bar, mobile-first step progress, pick walk progress, N of M picked, top-of-screen progress
ProgressBar.doNot: Do not animate width, height, or position — the fill is a scaleX transform with transformOrigin:'left' and w-full, gated by useReducedMotion. Law M1 bans layout tweens; transform was struck from that ban 2026-08-25, so the fill is legal only in that form. Duration is motionDuration.progressFill (100ms), never an inline literal. Progression is a COUNT, never a pointer position: pass satisfied-required-steps over total-required, so a pointer sitting on step 5 of 8 does not render 5/8. The `segments` prop is the touch/mobile-first face (operator 2026-09-14): N discrete increments, per-segment scaleX fill of the SAME law, aria progressbar wiring on the wrapper. Do not hand-roll a second segmented bar anywhere — kiosk, /m, or desk. A phone flow of NAMED steps (import, wizard) is MobileStepProgress — the same scaleX law with a 'Step N of M · label' caption and pressable completed steps (owner 2026-10-03).
ProgressBar.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG12 (segmented squares + a scaleX fill; M1 stands unamended), PG6 (percent-done is a count, never a position), PD1 (this file's width tween was the violation). Operator 2026-09-14: PG12's segmented face is now real via `segments`. Owner 2026-09-28: /m/pick paints it at the very top of the list and the walk; owner 2026-09-29: /m/qc too — one header, src/components/mobile/JobProgress.tsx (was PickProgress; `doneWord` names the count in the ARIA) — both faces carry role=progressbar + aria-valuenow/max.

StepProgressHeader.useWhen: step-flow header band, mobile-first wizard header, X close left + progress segments middle + n/N count right, kiosk pane form header, /m step flow header, Duolingo-style progress header
StepProgressHeader.doNot: Do not compose a step-flow header from a title band plus an inline meter — this band IS the header (operator 2026-09-14: 'all in one header, X top left, progress bar, one-out-of-ten top right'). Do not hand-roll the bar: it composes ProgressBar with `segments={total}`. The count counts COMPLETED units (PG6), never the index of the step in view. Do not add a pane title inside this band — the step eyebrow in the body names the current step. Back affordances inside a fixed-width form measure use this X when 'exit the flow' is the semantic; paged back-steps belong to the body, not this band.
StepProgressHeader.law: Operator 2026-09-14 — 'think Duolingo instead of text'; kiosk DS unification Phase 1. Composes ProgressBar (PG12/PG6/M1). Mounts: KioskRepairPane and KioskCartLedger, both via KioskPaneForm `progress`. Every mount's segment count is a gate table (repairStepGates, cartStepGates), never a step index.

StopSlider.useWhen: range slider, quantity slider, snapping slider, pick a count, how many labels, print run size, time to pack, drag to choose a value, stepped slider, discrete stops
StopSlider.doNot: Do not mount a native input type=range with accent-[...] — StopSlider is the one slider face: a large neutral track (bg-surface-sunken) with a dot at every stop, flush with the track (the SAME height, never taller, in both sizes; gray ahead, a deeper grey once reached), a grey fill, a flat solid grey thumb with no ring that darkens while pressed, a grey chosen-stop chip (never fill-info blue — the slider states a quantity, not a status), a focus ring for the keyboard only (:focus-visible, never on click), stop labels ABOVE the track (never under the thumb), and a 48px band (32px compact) that is the whole hit area. Values land on `stops` (ascending); position is the stop INDEX. Pass showStops={false} when the chip row would crowd (it auto-hides above 12 stops; dots hide above 24). Fill and thumb move by transform only (Law M1). Pair with DeferredQtyInput when an exact off-scale value must stay enterable.
StopSlider.law: Operator 2026-09-29 — the print-station quantity bar: cleaner, brighter and lighter, with a bigger click target, fixed at the root component. Operator 2026-10-03 (task principle P5, NN/g sliders): discrete stops drawn as dots on a large track, snap on release, label above, flat pressed face, keyboard-only focus ring — no blue ring on the thumb. Owner 2026-10-04 (root, every consumer): dots never taller than the track; fill / reached dots / thumb / chosen chip neutral grey. Mounts: FnskuQuantityPicker QuantityPicker, PackTimeSlider, MobileProductPackTimeCard, TotePrintRunFields, StockQtySlider, TaskDetailRail status, MobileTaskStatus.

ProcedureDeck.useWhen: station work surface, procedure steps, step column, work list, guided procedure, unbox steps, the surface an operator works a station from
ProcedureDeck.doNot: Do not gate capture on the active step. Evidence claims the step it belongs to, so the pointer is a HINT about what to capture next, never an authority that rejects input — scanning what step 5 wants while the pointer sits on step 2 satisfies step 5, and steps 3-4 stay open and unticked. Do not auto-complete the steps in between. Every step stays mounted from the first frame (existing invariant 1) — that is what makes a jumped-past open step visible without a scroll, so do not virtualize or collapse the list.
ProcedureDeck.law: docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG6 (evidence claims its own step; progression is non-linear), PG3 (evidence advances the pointer).

StepStateBadge.useWhen: step state mark, procedure step box, done/skipped/pending mark, checklist square
StepStateBadge.doNot: Do not make it clickable and do not render a rounded-full dot. A step is evidence-derived — a square that clicks to tick reintroduces the banned hand-ticked checklist. `skipped` keeps the chevron and never the check: a skip is a recorded waiver that a person looked and moved past, not a claim the work happened, and a required step skipped this way carries a deviation reason. One mark serves both ProcedureChecklist and ProcedureDeck; do not fork it per view.
StepStateBadge.law: File docblock (shape + evidence-derived). docs/warehouse-os/PROGRESSION-INTERVIEW-LEDGER.md — PG3 (evidence advances; tick is the fallback), PG8 (a skipped required step is a recorded deviation), PG1 (one derivation at two altitudes).

calendar.useWhen: calendar, date picker, day picker, month grid, shadcn calendar, 21st.dev calendar, react-day-picker
calendar.doNot: Do not import 'react-day-picker/style.css'. This file names every key in react-day-picker's UI enum, so no rdp-* class is emitted and the stylesheet is dead weight — while it was imported, the keys the old component missed (root, weeks, chevron) inherited library styling and .rdp-chevron{fill:var(--rdp-accent-color)} filled the nav chevron's stroked path into a solid blue triangle. Do not write data-[range-start=true] / data-[range-end=true] / data-[range-middle=true] chains: this repo is on react-day-picker v10, which emits none of those attributes — that is v9, and most shadcn range snippets in circulation are v9 or v8. Do not put raw text-blue-* inside an arbitrary variant ([&>button]: or hover:); the dark-scheme remap in styles/globals.css only rewrites the bare class, so it goes dark-on-dark — use a themed token. Do not drop relative or w-fit from the root, and do not simplify nav to inset-x-0 top-0: the p-3 root makes those offsets wrong by 12px vertically and 16px horizontally. Range picking is calendar-range-select, not this with mode="range" hand-styled. A full field (trigger + popover + Apply) is DateRangePickerField or DateRangePickerPill, not this bare primitive. Do not mount this as an inline table date editor; ship-by, due date, or a date in a cell uses DateRangePickerField variant="compact".
calendar.law: src/components/ui/calendar.tsx — shadcn/new-york lineage on react-day-picker v10, house tokens. Operator 2026-08-31: one calendar primitive; src/design-system/components/Calendar.tsx was deleted and all six consumers moved here.

calendar-range-select.useWhen: date range, range picker, from-to dates, period picker, week range, filter by date range, range calendar, start and end date
calendar-range-select.doNot: Do not hand-style a range on `calendar` — this file is the only place the range track is defined. range_middle must keep Tailwind's `!` suffix: in v10 a middle day is BOTH selected and range_middle and the two class strings land on the same cell, so equal specificity would let stylesheet order pick the winner. Do not move the endpoint pill off `selected` onto range_start/range_end — a half-picked range (from set, to open) sets only `selected`, because v10 requires both endpoints before it marks the range. Do not add a preset row above it; the four period chips were removed 2026-08-31 for restating the calendar and forcing the popover wider than the grid. This is the bare calendar — the trigger + popover + Apply field is DateRangePickerField variant="range", and the workbench-chrome pill is DateRangePickerPill. Do not drop this bare grid into a table cell. Cell / ship-by / due date is DateRangePickerField variant="compact".
calendar-range-select.law: src/components/ui/calendar-range-select.tsx — layers only range_start / range_end / range_middle over `calendar`. Operator 2026-08-31: ported from 21st.dev, retranslated from react-day-picker v9 to v10.

DateRangePickerField.useWhen: inline date edit, ship-by date, due date, data table date, pick a date in a cell, date under status, calendar date range display, date range field, replace input type=date, pick a date, single date
DateRangePickerField.doNot: Do not use InlineEditableValue for a date. Do not mount a native input type=date. Do not drop bare calendar or calendar-range-select into a table cell — those are the grid, this is the field. DateRangePickerPill is workbench header chrome only. variant="range" is the filter (presets + Apply + X, year in the face). variant="compact" is one civil day: calendar only, click commits, no X, no year, face is never blank; a due date passes optional `presets` (Today · Tomorrow · Next week chips above the month) and `onClear` (a Clear footer) — never a second picker beside it. DataTable ship-by is compact. Do not hand-roll a CompoundShipByEditor or a click-to-native-date control.
DateRangePickerField.law: src/design-system/components/DateRangePickerField.tsx. Operator 2026-09-01: DataTable / ship-by / inline date edit is variant=compact. Filter ranges stay variant=range.

InlineEditableValue.useWhen: inline text edit, pencil edit, click to retype a string, rename in place
InlineEditableValue.doNot: Not for dates. Ship-by, due date, and any inline date edit is DateRangePickerField variant="compact" (click commits, no X, no year).

DataTable.useWhen: DataTable, data table, spreadsheet grid, table vs card list, choosing a display method for rows or records, data table vs card list vs record surface, which list pattern fits this page, one-row table, small result set, queue vs ledger vs triage vs board, display-method decision, confidence meter for a display choice, dense sortable spreadsheet, rows and columns for a new page
DataTable.doNot: Code the scored winner, not the requested word: a page whose steady-state result set is one row renders a record surface (DetailSummaryCard mapper on DetailHubScreen, or RecordCard) instead of a table. When the top two candidates land in the same confidence tier, code nothing yet — present the ranked menu to the operator and implement their pick. Give every column a job: facts the operator never compares side-by-side move into a card's fact row (RecordCard facts), not a column. New surfaces mount the canonical DataTable with a direct TableSurfaceBinding; do not copy compound internals into a page.
DataTable.law: EXECUTABLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: src/lib/tables/display-method.ts (scoreDisplayMethod — per-fact score table, modifiers, confidence, decision; pinned by display-method.test.ts). Ask it, do not hand-score: MCP `ds_display_method` (facts: steadyRows, comparedFacts, verb, surface, optional shape, rowsPerScreen, urgencyBands, admin, statusGroups; verb monitor-pipeline + 6–12 statusGroups at a desk → column-board = ColumnBoard) or `node tools/design-mcp/ds.mjs display-method '<facts-json>'`. The decision (implement · implement-name-runner-up · ask) and the ask menu come back as data. The prose below is the formula it encodes; the module adds the SURFACE_LAW rule (desk-only tables and the column board lose 10 on a phone — lists on a phone are cards; a board is one column there). DISPLAY-METHOD DECISION FORMULA (owner 2026-09-29) — every page is different, so derive the display from facts about THIS page, never from the word table/grid/list in the request. STEP 1 — GATHER THE FACTS: steady-state row count; facts the operator compares side-by-side; record shape (one entity per row vs spanned/grouped rows); primary verb (scan-and-act, read-and-compare, edit-in-place, browse-and-drill); surface (desk, /m phone, kiosk); rows-per-screen need. STEP 2 — SCORE THE CANDIDATES (0–5 per fact, +2/−2 as noted): canonical DataTable (src/components/tables/DataTable.tsx with a direct TableSurfaceBinding; +2 when ≥5 compared columns AND desk-only AND sort/spreadsheet-edit verbs; −2 when steady-state rows ≤ 3); TriageCardList + RecordCard (src/design-system/components/triage-card-list, record-card; +2 when the verb is scan-and-act or the surface is /m; −1 when ≥5 compared columns); RecordLedger (append-style history reads); AdminTable (small admin CRUD, few rows, desk); TriageSections / TriageScrollLayout (urgency-banded queues); DetailHubScreen + DetailSummaryCard (+3 when steady-state rows ≤ 1). STEP 3 — CONFIDENCE METER: confidence = top score ÷ (5 × facts gathered). ≥ 0.75 HIGH — implement it; 0.50–0.74 MEDIUM — implement the top pick and name the runner-up in the change summary; < 0.50 LOW, or top two within one tier — ASK: present the menu (each candidate, its score, one line why, the trade it gives up, the single page fact that would settle it) and implement the operator's choice — a 30-second pick beats a rebuild.

LedgerGridColumnHeader.useWhen: column header, grid header row, spreadsheet header, select-all, resize column, auto-fit column width, double-click column edge, freeze columns, pin a column
LedgerGridColumnHeader.doNot: Do not cover or replace this row with row verbs. Morphing sits in the empty:hidden guest under this plate and pushes the sheet. Frozen select stays. Never paint actions on top of Order / Item / Dates.
LedgerGridColumnHeader.law: src/design-system/components/grid/LedgerGridColumnHeader.tsx + LedgerGrid.tsx action-row slot. Operator 2026-09-10: headers stay; actions drop below. SHEETS VERBS (owner 2026-10-04): drag the right-edge grip to resize; DOUBLE-CLICK it to fit the column to its widest rendered content (header + on-screen rows); `onFreezeColumn` adds a hover pin per header — freeze every column through this one, the current edge's pin unfreezes. Persistence and the model live in `useSheetColumns(storageKey, columns)` (src/components/tables/useSheetColumns.ts, localStorage) handed to DataTable's `columns` / `onResizeColumn` / `onFreezeColumn` — never a page-local resize.

SearchableSelectField.useWhen: sku type, platform, claim mode, location, inbound kind, flush compose combobox, not people, creatable combobox, add a new option inline (Add platform), create from the typed text

SearchableSelectField.law: src/design-system/components/SearchableSelectField.tsx. Operator 2026-09-11: staff is AssigneeCombobox. Operator 2026-09-25: evidence-column pickers (Platform, SKU bin) share the record trailing axis. Owner 2026-10-04: inline create is the `create={{ label, onCreate }}` row (always visible, last, hairline above; hidden while the query names an option exactly) — the host creates the row and picks it; never a second creatable picker. RecordCardMobile.doNot: Owner 2026-09-29: bin, platform and order number above the image (supersedes the 2026-09-28 F-pattern bin placement). TOP ROW, full card width, above the image: the BIN first (LocationBadge; 'No bin' → set-bin via location.onPress), then the platform (channel dot + name, FBA / Pickup badge) and the record ref (order number); the SLA pill at the far right of that row. No checkbox, no hover peek, no chips, no notes, no Take / Pass / verbs on the card. Do not branch inside RecordCard for a phone face, and do not hand-roll a phone order card: the family adapter fills a RecordCardMobileModel (orders: orderCardModel → orderRecordLine). Deadline ink and dot come from tokens/record-card.ts, shared with RecordCard. On the /m/pick order screen the dock's second verb is the SKU's bin — 'Pair bin' (no bin) / 'Update location' (has one), opening the set-bin sheet — never Unpick (owner 2026-09-29).
RecordCardMobile.law: src/design-system/components/record-card/RecordCardMobile.tsx (+ RecordSquarePhoto) + record-card-types.ts (RecordCardMobileModel) + tokens/record-card.ts. Orders adapter: src/components/mobile/picker/PickScreen.tsx (PickListCard); order screen photos: PickOrderScreen.tsx. QC adapter: src/lib/qc/qc-card-model.ts → src/components/mobile/qc/QcQueueScreen.tsx (owner 2026-09-29: `/m/qc` top row = bin or 'No bin' pair door · tier code (`code`, QC_QUEUE_TIER) · carton R- handle (`ref`) · age; body ends '→ Test' (`next`)). docs/design-system/BRIEF.md §14 (owner 2026-09-28: port the desk FBM → Allocate card to the phone; owner 2026-09-29: bin, platform and order number above the image; the product image on the order screen too).

TriageCardList.doNot: Status sections use sections="by-state" with family.state; see docs/design-system/HANDOFF-record-card-families.md (Laws). CREATE is the position an untouched control shows, which is honest only because `null` also posts as create (kioskTicketWork) and counts as settled (isKioskTicketChoiceSettled); the HALF-FINISHED state — slid to Link with nothing picked — is what still refuses the commit. IosBar.doNot: Do not stack a second header row, put the ✕ under the title, or hand-roll a bordered icon button: trailing items are IosBarButton (44px, borderless glass circle) in two groups — tools (IosMoreMenu, live state) then close. IosMoreMenu.useWhen: three dots, ellipsis menu, more button, overflow menu, secondary actions, add person behind a menu, hide actions, pull-down menu, kebab, actions menu on a record
IosMoreMenu.doNot: Do not put the one primary verb in it, list fewer than three items, or run a destructive item straight from the menu (confirm in ConfirmSheet). IosMoreMenu.law: src/components/mobile/ios/IosMoreMenu.tsx on the house DropdownMenu — Apple HIG Pull-down buttons + Menus (researched 2026-10-03); owner 2026-10-03: 'adding staff must be behind the three dots'. The task sheet (MobileTaskSheet) is the reference composition.

PastedListPage.useWhen: pasted list full screen, see every pasted number with all its facts, bulk lookup results page, delivered unboxed who unboxed for many numbers, /search/list
PastedListPage.doNot: Do not paint the full list as an overlay over the page or a bigger popover — it is its own route (`pastedListHref`), Esc returns to `back`. Do not add a second locate or a per-locator lookup: buckets are the bar's `useLocatedList` answer; receiving facts are the Inbound ledger's reads. Do not invent columns for facts no client read returns (outbound ship-by / shipped / packer today). Do not hard-code '/search/list' — use the route tree's `SEARCH_PATHS` / `pastedListHref`. Do not put a find field in the page body — the sidebar field is the one Find. Do not wrap a cell or pad columns apart: one line, ellipsis, hairline dividers. Do not open a record on a row press — a press copies the cell. Do not bind ⌘+ / ⌘− (the browser's zoom). Do not paint units orange or call a number short/over: the units are PO-line sums, green once unboxed.
PastedListPage.law: src/app/search/list/page.tsx (DeskPageLayout title 'Pasted list', measure full) → src/components/search/pasted-list/PastedListPage.tsx + PastedListGridRow.tsx + pasted-list-table.ts (owner 2026-10-04). URL: `?refs=` (comma-joined, parseRefInParam — the bar's parse and cap), `?locator=` (inbound | outbound | everywhere), `?status=` (one bucket id, own or `<locator>:<id>`, or `nowhere`), `?back=`. CONTROLS (owner ruling A4, 2026-10-04 — supersedes the same day's body chip row): the status buckets (bare status words + counts, Not found a facet) and the sort are declared in this page's contextual sidebar (NAV_PAGE_DECLS + its facet context) writing `?status=` and the sort param — never BulkStatusChips / BulkSortChips in the page body (ledger `body-status-chip-rails`; loop rule `layout.sidebar-owns-table-controls`). The body's top row (GOOGLE-SHEETS LAYOUT) carries only verbs: Copy shown (⌘⌥C) · Export (CSV of exactly the columns and rows on screen, screen order, `pastedListCellText` → downloadExport) · Recheck all · Back (Esc). NO find field in the page: its Find is the sidebar field (`NAV_PAGE_DECLS.search`, desk-store keyed by the path), matched over every column's text. Columns: # · Number (frozen) · Status · Product title · PO · Vendor · Delivered · Unboxed (+who) · Units · Detail; sheet density (4px side pad, 2px top/bottom, hairline column dividers, one line, ellipsis + full text on hover); the grid scrolls both ways under its sticky header; resize / double-click fit / freeze from the header persist via `useSheetColumns(PASTED_LIST_LAYOUT_KEY)`. Keys (`?` sheet group 'Pasted list'): ↑↓/J K, ↵ open (recordHref, else the bucket's list narrowed to it), R recheck, ⌘C copy, ⌘⌥C copy shown, O / S sort, Esc back. ROUND 2026-10-04b: Back is the FIRST element of the title line (DeskPageLayout `titleLead` → PastedListBack; Esc shares `usePastedListBack`). Zoom − / % / + sit top-right of the verb row: 80·90·100·110·125·150%, persisted with the layout (`useSheetColumns` → `zoom`, `stepZoom`), applied as `--cf-density` on the sheet so role type, rem tracks, resized widths (kept at 100%) and the zoom-scaled cell padding move together; ⌘+ / ⌘− stay the browser's. Every row shows (DataTable `unpaged`, virtualized). A press on a cell COPIES its text (toast 'Copied <value>' + a findCellCopied wash); the row never opens on a press — the record opens from the hover ExternalLink icon in the Number cell, or Enter / O on the cursor row (O no longer sorts here). Unboxed and Delivered read date + time (formatMonthDayTimePST, warehouse time) + StaffCell. Units (PastedListUnits): received/expected over the PO lines, GREEN when the number is unboxed (facts.unboxedAt), muted otherwise, a 2px scaleX underline in the same tone, a title naming the source — never 'short'/'over' wording, never orange. A number the paste carried more than once wears ×N in its Number cell (`BulkList.repeats` → `?rep=`). Delivered-not-unboxed rows lead their Detail with 'Nd since delivered' (amber ≥2, red ≥5).
